maria (eng-runtime): Heads-up: since yesterday's rollout we're seeing a steady drop in prefix/prompt cache hit-rate for chat-prod-1 and a couple of GPU OOM spikes. Hit-rate went from ~78% -> ~54% over 6 hours, GPU resident mem +18%, and memory fragmentation metric jumped. Trying to collect notes here so we can triage.

jon (eng-runtime): I saw the same on our perf dashboard. Quick paste of today: 
```
prefix_cache_hits_total: 1.2M
prefix_cache_misses_total: 1.0M
prefix_cache_resident_bytes: 3123456789
prefix_cache_frag_ratio: 0.27
kv_inserts/s (10m): 4200 -> baseline 900
```
Looks like insert rate spiked which explains growth.

sachin (eng-ml): My profiler from the serving nodes shows two hot changes: 1) keying logic started including a per-request ephemeral nonce in the cache key for some routes (accidentally) so we never hit; 2) kernel selection change: for sequence lengths > 1024 the runtime switched to the large GEMM path that allocates a bigger temp buffer, pushing memory high.

maria (eng-runtime): gah - that nonce thing matches a PR I reviewed. @jon can you grep which routes have the new keying? I can roll a fix to normalize keys if it's that.

jon (eng-runtime): I already did a quick scan. Problematic routes: /chat/stream and /chat/batch when customer_session_id is present we appended `:sess=<uuid>` to the prefix key. Suggestion: normalize to stable session bucket instead of raw uuid, e.g. `sess=bucket(<id>,128)` or drop entirely for prompt-prefix keying. Small snippet: 
```
// bad
key := fmt.Sprintf("%s|sess=%s|v=%d", prompt, sessionID, modelVersion)
// normalized
key := fmt.Sprintf("%s|sess_bucket=%d|v=%d", prompt, sessionHash%128, modelVersion)
```
Dropping nonce reduces cardinality and should raise hit-rate quickly.

olivia (eng-sre): On eviction/TTL: we currently use a single global LRU with TTL=5m for all prefixes. Two ideas: 1) tier TTLs by route (chat-short:30s, chat-long:10m, reranker:1h) and 2) enforce separate CPU/GPU budgets so GPU cache can't balloon because GPU memory is scarcer. Proposed eviction YAML: 
```
prefix_cache:
  default_ttl_s: 300
  route_ttl:
    "/chat/short": 30
    "/chat/long": 600
    "/rerank": 3600
  gpu_budget_bytes: 8GB
  cpu_budget_bytes: 64GB
  policy: size_and_age_lru
```
Also we should probe compaction: run `kv-compact --shard=all --threshold=0.2` on low-traffic window to reduce fragmentation.

sachin (eng-ml): About kernel selection: lowering threshold for big GEMM to 800 cut peak temp buffer size ~22% in my synthetic runs. We can make the threshold dynamic: pick kernel based on median seq length in the pending batch rather than static threshold. Pseudo-config: `kernel_selection: per_batch_median_threshold: 800`.

maria (eng-runtime): Batching heuristics are related. If we let batches grow (max_batch_tokens large) we may pick larger kernels more often. Suggest temporary rollback: set max_batch_tokens=4096 and batch_wait_ms=12 to limit growth while we fix keying.

jon (eng-runtime): Agreed. I'll open a canary with: 
```
deploy cfg set serving.batch.max_batch_tokens=4096
deploy cfg set serving.batch.batch_wait_ms=12
rollout canary chat-prod-1 10%
```
And I'll push the key normalization hotfix to canary as well.

olivia (eng-sre): Action items: 
- normalize keys to reduce cardinality (owner: @jon)
- per-route TTLs + GPU/CPU budgets + compaction (owner: @olivia)
- adjust kernel threshold (owner: @sachin)
- temporary batching caps and canary rollout (owner: @jon)
Set deadlines: try canary today, cluster-wide next deploy if stable.

maria (eng-runtime): One more metric we should add now before the cluster-wide: `prefix_cardinality_by_route` so we can see which routes drove cardinality explosion. Please add that to the alert dashboard.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for chat-prod-1 -> 10% (by @jon) :rocket:

jon (eng-runtime): I pushed key normalization to canary and started ingesting prefix_cardinality_by_route. Early numbers at +30m: hit-rate up to 71% on canary nodes, GPU resident memory down ~9%. We'll let it run another hour then evaluate.

maria (eng-runtime): great, keep updates here. If canary stabilizes we follow with TTL per-route + eviction budgets. If we still see tail OOMs after that, we'll enable background compaction and consider short-circuiting the large GEMM path for high-frag hosts.

olivia (eng-sre): noted. scheduling kv-compact on low-traffic window tonight 02:00 UTC, will monitor fragmentation metrics.

sachin (eng-ml): I'll prepare the kernel threshold PR and include telemetry for kernel_choice_count so we can correlate kernel switches with mem spikes.

jon (eng-runtime): +1. Will post canary results in 60-90m. :thumbsup:

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks everyone.
